title: Cardinal-smallness consequences for a perfect derived class
statement: If S in a Grothendieck derived category is essentially small, replete and triangulated, is closed under coproducts indexed by types of cardinality less than a regular cardinal alpha, and every object of S is alpha-presentable, then componentwise surjectivity on Hom from S survives every v-small coproduct and every map from an object of S to a coproduct of S-objects factors through a subcoproduct in S.

source.place: Bounded-subcoproduct factorization and perfectness: Krause Localization theory Sections 6.2-6.3 and Proposition 6.8.1.

proof.text: Factor a map from an alpha-presentable object through a finite subcoproduct of the target family, using the finite-support factorization lemma.

For a finite subcoproduct, lift each component through the given componentwise surjections and reassemble the lifts by the finite biproduct lemma; transport the lift along the subcoproduct inclusions.
Apply the factorization lemma to a map into a coproduct of S-objects and use closure of S under subcoproducts.

proof_origin.place: Formal cardinal-smallness consequences, reduced to finite-support and finite-biproduct lemmas.

theorem derived_perfectSmallClass_properties
    {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v} A] [HasDerivedCategory.{v} A]
    (S : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory A)) (α : Cardinal.{v}) [Fact α.IsRegular]
    [ObjectProperty.EssentiallySmall.{v} S]
    [S.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms] [S.IsTriangulated]
    (hSsum : ∀ (I : Type v) (Y : I → DerivedCategory A), HasCardinalLT I α →
      (∀ i, S (Y i)) → S (∐ Y))
    (hcompact : ∀ U, S U → IsCardinalPresentable U α) :
    (∀ (I : Type v) (X Y : I → DerivedCategory A) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ Y i),
      (∀ i U, S U → Function.Surjective (fun g : U ⟶ X i ↦ g ≫ f i)) →
      ∀ U, S U → Function.Surjective
        (fun g : U ⟶ ∐ X ↦ g ≫ Limits.Sigma.map f)) ∧
    (∀ (I : Type v) (Y : I → DerivedCategory A), (∀ i, S (Y i)) →
      ∀ (U : DerivedCategory A), S U → ∀ f : U ⟶ ∐ Y,
      ∃ (J : Type v) (a : J → I), S (∐ fun j ↦ Y (a j)) ∧
        ∃ g : U ⟶ ∐ fun j ↦ Y (a j),
          g ≫ Sigma.desc (fun j ↦ Sigma.ι Y (a j)) = f)
